opening: I am writing to apply for the AI Engineer role at Lleverage. Your line that AI is only useful when it actually fits into daily operations is the whole job as far as I am concerned, and it is the reason I am applying here rather than to a research-flavoured role. I have spent three years on the unglamorous side of that sentence: getting models into workflows that people already had, and dealing with what happens when the model does not behave.
role_specific: You list a background in SaaS or low-code platforms as a nice to have. That is my actual background rather than a bonus. At FlowSpace I inherited a Bubble.io product and led its migration to Next.js and Laravel on a live system while it grew from 2,000 to over 4,500 active users, so I have seen both sides of the low-code-to-real-code line that your product sits on. I build agents and automated workflows in n8n and by calling APIs directly, including the support AI agents at FlowSpace and an AI data parsing tool for UltraStrategy built in n8n with Eden AI. I have done RAG retrieval over real document sets, function calling and structured outputs against OpenAI and Anthropic, and the TypeScript and Next.js work you need for the surrounding product.
closing: The honest gaps: I have not fine-tuned models, my LLM evaluation has been hand-built regression checks rather than a proper framework with defined metrics, and my vector search work has been through managed tooling rather than running the database myself. I have about three years in and no CS degree. If the bar here is a founding-engineer-level AI specialist then I am not that, and I would rather say so than waste an interview. If what you need is someone who has repeatedly shipped this exact category of thing into production, I would like to talk.
